name: shared-pipeline
instruction: Review the target file for duplicated ownership of the same domain behavior or metadata. Read root AGENTS.md, CONTEXT.md, and the relevant sibling implementations and callers. Look for competing tool metadata, permissions or write classifications, prefab and typed-network identity, recording validation, event projections, or result interpretation that must remain consistent across consumers. For each head, built-in or external, connection tests and live runs should share connection construction and the selected settings/request path. A test probes edited settings without applying them; a running session keeps its applied snapshot. Report a separate hard-coded client, provider default, model, endpoint, or launch path that causes a test to verify a different connection than the selected one. A connection probe may use a short prompt without running a full city turn; protocol-specific transport remains in its adapter. Report only when you can name the authoritative source or existing shared pipeline, the duplicate implementation, and a concrete divergence or maintenance obligation. Prefer one owner with multiple consumers; place construction search and recovery inside the building or linear-network write. A building write and a linear-network write each remain one model-facing verb for their domain. Similar-looking code for genuinely different native operations, provider protocols, display projections, or independent tests need not be merged. Do not demand a generic framework, new public interface, or abstraction solely because two snippets have similar syntax. Point to the target implementation that duplicates knowledge and identify the sibling evidence. Report no finding when there is no demonstrated shared invariant.
